statement.text:
Let Γ be a connected undirected graph without loops or multiple edges and
suppose that the automorphism group Aut(Γ) acts transitively on the vertex set of Γ.
Is it true that at least one of the following assertions holds?
    1. The stabilizer of a vertex of Γ in Aut(Γ) is finite.
    2. The group Aut(Γ) as a permutation group on the vertex set of Γ admits an
imprimitivity system σ with finite blocks for which the stabilizer of a vertex of the
factor-graph Γ/σ in Aut(Γ/σ) is finite.
    3. There exists a natural number n such that the graph obtained from Γ by adding
edges joining distinct vertices the distance between which in Γ is at most n contains
a regular tree of valency 3.                                           V. I. Trofimov
